items.headline: FMRB executive order post-briefing record
items.diff_narrative: Saturday opened the post-briefing record with the classified-annex follow-up question set transmitted to the eight-witness slate and the ten-business-day response clock starting. Sunday advances that clock into its second calendar day and adds a procedural detail: NIST Director Locascio's office and the CISA Director's office have filed early acknowledgements of receipt, though no substantive responses landed over the business-quiet weekend. The Just Security no-objection reading on the signing-window blocker and the OSTP no-signing-before-May-22 line both carry forward unchanged, and the House parallel 30-day technical-review joint-resolution draft still circulates with no weekend markup notice.

items.headline: Cyber-evaluation reciprocity perimeter at fifteen jurisdictions
items.diff_narrative: Saturday converted Qatar's adjacent-track interest into a formal exploratory-observer entry, pushing the perimeter to fifteen named candidates. Sunday holds that count flat with no fresh entry and moves the substance to schema mechanics: the OECD GENAI secretariat reports member-state comment submissions on the finalized attestation field schema have crossed the halfway mark of the named candidate cohort, on schedule for the June 2-6 plenary adoption target. Qatar's 270-day national-consultation window enters its first weekend, and no third Gulf Cooperation Council member has signalled interest.

items.headline: n8n CVE-2026-21858 exposure taper before May 21 deadline
items.diff_narrative: The day-sixteen scan rolls to day-seventeen with the federal-civilian remediation deadline stepping from T-minus-five to T-minus-four business days. Internet-exposed pre-1.121.0 instances continue the descent from roughly 2,180 to 1,920, the residual unpatched long-tail share eases from 16 percent to about 14 percent, and Censys exploitation telemetry moderates further from 1.6x to roughly 1.4x baseline on the scheduled weekend taper. The CISA federal-civilian operational directive carrying the eleven-CVE taxonomy, which cleared the OMB queue Friday, remains on track for early-new-week publication.

items.headline: Unified five-surface loader-verification model closes empirically
items.diff_narrative: Saturday established the formal settling point: arxiv 2605.07241 folded the eleven-CVE taxonomy into a single five-surface verification model with Python and Rust reference implementations. Sunday closes the line empirically with a fresh companion release, arxiv 2605.07412, an empirical-evaluation note that runs the consolidated reference implementations against all eleven catalogued CVE patterns, reports a full pass on the compositional safety theorems, and adds a per-surface micro-benchmark showing the signed-checkpoint and manifest-allowlist paths add low single-digit-percentage cold-start overhead. Simon Willison characterizes the pair as a verified reference plus a measured overhead budget for the mid-June framework default; the framework maintainer cohort's coordinated commitment now points at a single agreed baseline.

items.headline: MCP-server attack-surface telemetry holds above 90 percent
items.diff_narrative: Saturday held cross-vendor agentic-AI control-plane visibility above the 90 percent threshold. Sunday holds that line with no fresh disclosure: the median provisioning-to-first-credential-extraction time on unprotected estates holds at 5 minutes for a sixth consecutive day, the unprotected-versus-protected gap stays near 67x, and Defender-for-Cloud quarantine on net-new MCP servers ticks from 46 percent to 47 percent — a seventh consecutive day of expansion. Cisco-Astrix identity-gateway tenancy edges to roughly 2,390 and Akamai SkyAtlas MCP-firewall to roughly 1,375.

items.headline: Cerebras CBRS sell-side hold-steady into the new trading week
items.diff_narrative: Saturday was a sell-side weekend-coverage cycle with no fresh tape after Friday's $198.60 four-consolidation-day close. Sunday is a second business-quiet hold: the five-desk spread carries forward unchanged inside the roughly $185-to-$235 band, institutional-buyside net position holds near 37 percent of float, and the Saudi Aramco Digital MoU and Saudi PIF contingent-secondary windows hold. The new detail is forward-looking — the desk preview cohort flags Monday's open as the first re-rating opportunity for the four-day consolidation base.

items.headline: Mag-7 print-cycle preview ahead of the May 21 Alphabet analyst day
items.diff_narrative: The Alphabet analyst day steps from Saturday's T-minus-five to T-minus-four calendar days. The six-desk preview cohort holds the Alphabet Q2 AI Services 10-Q footnote breakout probability at 87 percent, now naming Monday's open as the start of the analyst-day run-up window. On the AI-accelerator IPO track, Tenstorrent's first-round comment-letter substantive response sits in the standard staff-review interval ahead of a likely second-round letter with the early-August public-filing target held, and SambaNova's bookrunner roster holds at six with the confidential-submission target firmed to the final week of June.

items.headline: Anthropic Claude Code 3.0 registry growth normalization
items.diff_narrative: Day nine rolls to day ten with the second-week growth normalization continuing — published skills rise from roughly 27,640 to 29,180 (+5.6 percent, a fourth consecutive sub-7-percent reading) and auto-quarantined Mythos-class skills go from 62 to 65. The Mythos-Preview gated cohort holds at 64 enterprise customers with no weekend signings, and the verification harness's cross-tenant compositional safety check holds under 55 seconds. The Decoder adds that the gated cohort's Continental European and Nordic defense base is unchanged ahead of an expected resumption of enterprise signings in the new week.

items.headline: Open-source serving stacks frozen before the Monday vLLM stable cut
items.diff_narrative: Saturday was a hold-steady benchmark cycle ahead of the Monday May 18 vLLM v0.11.4 stable cut. Sunday confirms the v0.11.4 release branch is now frozen for that targeted Monday cut, with the final tag expected to publish at the start of the new week. The Yotta Labs throughput gap holds near 2.7 percent — vLLM v0.11.4-rc2 at roughly 18,990 tok/s versus SGLang RadixArk v0.5.9 at roughly 19,510 tok/s, effectively flat — and Cloudflare Infire holds L40S edge-tier parity at 1.00x.

items.headline: Tenstorrent Galaxy rack shipments edge to 168 racks
items.diff_narrative: Saturday's small weekend top-up lifted cumulative Wormhole Galaxy racks to roughly 162. Sunday adds another weekend top-up bringing the cumulative count to roughly 168 against the 280-rack first-half target — about 60 percent fulfilled — with additions across the North American neocloud cohort plus a small increment to Yotta Labs India, and the European and Latin American sovereign-cloud cohorts holding. AMD's Helios plus MI450 commitment book holds near 10.1GW with no fresh weekend commitment, and Datacenter Dynamics frames the 60 percent capacity-fulfillment curve as the revenue-traction anchor the Tenstorrent confidential S-1 is expected to lean on.

items.headline: Tesla Optimus Gen 3 holds 84 active units at Fremont
items.diff_narrative: Saturday activated a seventh cohort to reach 84 active units. Sunday holds that count flat with no eighth cohort activated over the business-quiet weekend — 35 percent of the disclosed 240-unit allocation reached, cycle-time steady at a roughly 1.03x human-baseline envelope. A Sunday clip shows a second weekend-shift three-line cross-cell coordination run across the Fremont automotive, sub-assembly, and battery-module lines with roughly thirty-four units, a small extension of Saturday's first run. The Stellantis Detroit (June 8) and Volkswagen Wolfsburg (June 22) activation dates hold.

items.headline: Boston Dynamics Atlas extends to a 96-hour continuous-operation milestone
items.diff_narrative: BMW Group's Spartanburg 30-unit Atlas pilot advances from Saturday's first North American 72-hour continuous-operation milestone to a first North American 96-hour milestone on the under-body conveyor task with zero MTBF-impacting incidents. Volkswagen Wolfsburg's Atlas pilot holds at roughly 80 units, the humanoid league-table OEM-adopter roster holds at six, and Hyundai Metaplant's Dangjin rolling-mill cycle-time improvement holds near 5.1 percent for a sixth consecutive within-band day, with the policy-distillation pipeline still running on the Tenstorrent Galaxy plus Unsloth router-only stack.
